paper.title: Estimating ETS parameters: smooth and statsforecast on simulated data

definitions.definition: smooth 1.2.0 ES(model=<form>, initial='optimal', loss='likelihood', bounds='usual'); smoothing parameters estimated by maximum likelihood with the initial states estimated jointly.
smooth 1.2.0 ES(model=<form>, initial='backcasting', loss='likelihood', bounds='usual'): smooth's default; initial states obtained by backcasting, only smoothing parameters optimised.

statsforecast 2.1.1 AutoETS(season_length=m, model=<form>, damped=False) with the form fixed to the generating one (no selection); maximum likelihood with optimised initial states; bounds lower 1e-4, upper 0.9999 for alpha, beta, gamma, beta<=alpha, gamma<=1-alpha, and admissibility.

Innovations ETS with additive Gaussian errors, sigma=1, started from l0=100, b0=1, s_j=10 sin(2 pi j/12), no burn-in; ETS(A,N,N) alpha 0.1 and 0.5; ETS(A,A,N) (alpha,beta) (0.3,0.05) and (0.5,0.2); ETS(A,N,A) m=12 (alpha,gamma)=(0.2,0.1); lengths 50,100,250,500; R replicates per cell.
Mean over successful replicates of (estimate minus true value) of a smoothing parameter.
Square root of the mean over successful replicates of the squared (estimate minus true value) of a smoothing parameter.
Mean over successful replicates of the absolute value of (estimate minus true value) of a smoothing parameter.
The RMSE of an estimator falls towards zero as series length T grows; here assessed on T in {50,100,250,500} by the RMSE at T=500 against the RMSE at T=50 and the trend across the four lengths.

claims.statement: With optimised initial states, [[D1:smooth ES]] and [[D3:statsforecast AutoETS]] have [[D6:RMSE]] of the alpha, beta and gamma estimates within 10% of each other (ratio between 0.9 and 1.1) in every setting and length of [[D4:the ETS data generating processes]].

claims.statement: At T=50, [[D2:smooth ES with backcasting]] has a lower [[D6:RMSE]] of the smoothing parameter estimates than [[D1:smooth ES with optimised initials]] in most (at least 6 of 8) parameter-setting cells of [[D4:the ETS data generating processes]].

n_bc.variable: cells at T=50 with lower RMSE for smooth ES backcasting than optimised initials

claims.statement: For each of the three arms, the [[D6:RMSE]] of every smoothing parameter estimate is lower at T=500 than at T=50, in all 8 parameter-setting cells of [[D4:the ETS data generating processes]] ([[D8:consistency]]).

claims.statement: The two implementations optimise comparable objectives: both maximise the Gaussian likelihood of the innovations form (smooth loss='likelihood', statsforecast opt_crit='lik'), so differences in estimates come from optimiser, bounds and initial-state handling.

alpha, beta, gamma have the same meaning in both packages (innovations/error-correction form, b_t=b_{t-1}+beta*e_t, s_t=s_{t-m}+gamma*e_t), so estimates are compared to the true values without conversion; to be checked by the data (bias of both near zero at T=500) not assumed unchecked.

evidence.description: Lab runs RN2 under plan PL1. Design: One run of claimset-code/ets-estimation/sim.py --seed 20261111 --R 300 --T 50 100 250 500. Five generating processes (ETS(A,N,N) alpha 0.1 and 0.5; ETS(A,A,N) (alpha,beta) (0.3,0.05) and (0.5,0.2); ETS(A,N,A) m=12 (alpha,gamma)=(0.2,0.1)), additive Gaussian errors sigma=1, l0=100, b0=1, s_j=10 sin(2 pi j/12), no burn-in, 300 replicates per process and length, series simulated with numpy default_rng(SeedSequence([20261111, process index, T])), the same series fitted by all three arms (smooth ES optimised initials, smooth ES backcasting, statsforecast AutoETS), each with the generating form fixed (no selection). Comparability as in note NT1. Analysis: Per arm, process, parameter and T: bias, RMSE and MAE of estimate minus true value over successful fits; failed fits and estimates on a bound (within 1e-3) are counted. Decision quantities: (a) over the 32 cells (8 parameter-process cells x 4 lengths) the minimum and maximum of RMSE(smooth ES optimised initials)/RMSE(statsforecast AutoETS); (b) the number of the 8 parameter-process cells at T=50 where RMSE(smooth backcasting) < RMSE(smooth optimised); (c) per arm the number of the 8 cells where RMSE at T=500 is not below RMSE at T=50. No inferential test: results are descriptive summaries of simulation output under fixed seeds. Bias, MAE and the cell-level numbers beyond these are reported as descriptive results.
